extracted.intended_audience: rail industry stakeholders (railroads, locomotive manufacturers/maintainers), regulatory/legal counsel, and members of the public who may submit comments
extracted.subtask_description: A Federal Railroad Administration notice of proposed rulemaking to amend 49 CFR 229.73 setting numeric maximum allowable diameter variation between locomotive wheel sets, distinguishing limits by traction motor technology and axle type; includes administrative instructions for submitting comments and the agency's regulatory analyses. Useful for parties drafting technical or legal comments or assessing compliance implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum variation — powered axles on AC locomotives (single axle control)
rubrics_metrics.description: For wheel sets on locomotives equipped with alternating current traction motors that utilize individual truck or single axle control technology: powered axles, 1 1/2 inches, with or without shims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FRA proposes allowing a larger maximum variation (1.5 inches) for AC locomotives using single-axle control because AC traction motor technology applies voltage and controls current precisely to each wheel set, reducing wheel-size-variation-triggered slip corrections. This is intended to accommodate new technology while maintaining safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption — non-powered axles on AC locomotives (middle axle exemption)
rubrics_metrics.description: For wheel sets on locomotives equipped with alternating current traction motors that utilize individual truck or single axle control technology: Non-powered axles in the middle of two powered axles are not subject to the 1 1/2 inch restriction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FRA does not expect wheel variation on non-powered middle axles to have a significant impact on truck dynamics for AC locomotives with single-axle control, so the proposed revision would eliminate the restriction for those axles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum variation — within same three-powered-axle truck (DC locomotives)
rubrics_metrics.description: For wheel sets on locomotives equipped with direct current traction motors: Within the same three-powered-axle truck, 3/4 inch, except that when shims are used at the journal box springs to compensate for wheel diameter variation, the maximum variation may not exceed 1 1/4 inches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The tighter 3/4-inch limit (or up to 1.25 inches with shims) remains for older DC-equipped locomotives because DC traction systems experience current imbalance and wheel-slip-correction behavior when wheel diameters vary; shims permit a limited additional tolerance when used to compensate for variation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum variation — on different trucks (DC locomotives)
rubrics_metrics.description: For wheel sets on locomotives equipped with direct current traction motors: On different trucks on a locomotive that has three-powered-axle trucks, 1 1/4 inches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Existing rule retained for inter-truck wheel set variation on DC-equipped locomotives; recognizes differing impacts on dynamics between within-truck and between-truck wheel differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of measured quantity (wheel set diameter variation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The maximum variation in the diameter between any two wheel sets is defined as the variation between the average diameter of the two wheels on an axle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All numeric limits in §229.73(b) apply to the average diameter of the two wheels on an axle (i.e., the wheel set), not to individual wheel measurements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety rationale — when wheel-size variation is a concern
rubrics_metrics.description: Excessive wheel size variation is a safety concern because it can affect wheel slip, truck dynamics, and weight distribution, potentially leading to reduced ability of trucks to absorb shifting loads and increasing derailment risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble contrasts DC and AC traction motor behavior: DC traction can produce current imbalance and unnecessary wheel-slip corrections (sanding, removing tractive effort) when wheel diameters vary; AC traction with single-axle control reduces wheel-size-variation-triggered corrections but still requires limits to preserve truck dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment submission content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions must include the agency name, docket number (FRA-2025-0126), and Regulatory Identification Number (RIN 2130-AD50).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should be submitted via https://www.regulations.gov following the online instructions. FRA will post all comments without change (including any personal information). If submitting proprietary or confidential information, contact the agency for alternate submission instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment procedural requirements — method and posting
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments related to Docket No. FRA-2025-0126 may be submitted via Regulations.gov; all comments received will be posted without change to Regulations.gov and may include personal information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations.gov instructions must be followed to file comments and to access the docket to read background documents or previously submitted comments. FRA may redact or withhold certain submissions or portions at its discretion, and some submitted comments may not be available to be read until approved by the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments on the proposed rule must be received by September 2, 2025; FRA may consider comments received after that date only to the extent practicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeliness affects consideration; late submissions may be considered but are not guaranteed to be considered fully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Flexibility Act consideration / small entity analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Regulatory Flexibility Act, agencies must consider effects of regulatory actions on small entities and minimize significant economic impacts; an analysis is not required if the head of the agency certifies that the rule would not have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FRA certifies this proposed rule would not have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities because it offers flexibilities and does not preclude existing compliant practices; FRA also invites small entities to consult the listed contact if they have questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Order 14192 implementation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: E.O. 14192 requires that for each new regulatory action issued at least ten prior regulations be identified for elimination and defines 'deregulatory action' versus 'regulatory action'; a deregulatory action is one finalized with total costs less than zero.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FRA states the proposed rule is expected to have total costs less than zero and would be considered an E.O. 14192 deregulatory action upon issuance of a final rule, and requests comment on the extent of cost savings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act status
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule contains no new information collection requirements under the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 (44 U.S.C. 3501-3520).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No OMB control number or new paperwork burden results from this rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEPA treatment — categorical exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: FRA has analyzed the rule under NEPA and determined it is categorically excluded pursuant to 23 CFR 771.118(c)(4) for planning and administrative activities such as promulgation of rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FRA does not anticipate environmental impacts and states no unusual or extraordinary circumstances are present that would require further NEPA review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfunded Mandates threshold assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: This proposed rule would not result in aggregate expenditures of $100,000,000 or more (adjusted for inflation) by State, local, or Tribal governments, or the private sector in any one year, so no written statement under the Unfunded Mandates Reform Act is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FRA evaluated the economic impact relative to the statutory threshold and concluded the rule does not trigger UNMRA requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Energy impact (E.O. 13211) assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: FRA evaluated the proposed rule under E.O. 13211 and determined it is not a 'significant energy action' requiring a Statement of Energy Effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No significant effects on energy supply, distribution, or use are anticipated from this rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tribal consultation (E.O. 13175) assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: FRA evaluated this rule under E.O. 13175 and determined it would not have a substantial direct effect on Indian tribes, would not impose substantial direct compliance costs on tribal governments, and would not preempt tribal laws; consultation requirements do not apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FRA concluded no tribal summary impact statement is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy Act and comment identification guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 5 U.S.C. 553(c), DOT solicits comments and posts them to Regulations.gov; to facilitate tracking, commenters are encouraged to provide their name or organization though submission of names is optional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Privacy Act system of records DOT/ALL-14 FDMS applies; commenters wishing to submit proprietary/confidential information should contact the agency for alternate submission instructions to avoid public posting of such material.
